summary: Rerank endpoint returns intermittent 500s on large batches (likely payload/tokenization memory spike)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports /v1/rerank returns 500 Internal Server Error when submitting large batches (many documents or large doc texts). Smaller batches succeed.

Customer impact
- Aurora Search uses rerank for search results ordering. Failures cause degraded relevance and increased latency due to retries/fallback.
- Impact is intermittent but reproducible with large payloads. Customer reports this started ~2026-02-11.

Environment
- Tier: self_serve (Hosted API)
- Env: prod
- Regions observed: us-east (primary), eu-west (observed once)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/rerank
- SDK: customer calling REST directly (not Redwood SDK)

Symptoms
- HTTP 500 with JSON error body similar to:
  {"error":{"message":"Internal error","type":"server_error","request_id":"req_01HT2ZK8Y4M6J4A8X9W2"}}
- Typical request latency before failure: 6–15s
- Customer notes failures correlate with:
  - documents >= ~150 per request, AND/OR
  - document text lengths 5–10KB each

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided)
1) POST /v1/rerank with:
   - query length: ~600–1500 chars
   - documents: 180–260 items
   - per-document text length: ~4–9KB
2) Observe 500 within ~10s.
3) Retry the same payload: may succeed once, then fail again.
4) Split documents into chunks of 25–50: consistently succeeds.

Repro payload size hints (sanitized)
- Case A (fails ~60%): 220 docs, avg doc 6.3KB, total request body ~1.6MB
- Case B (succeeds 100%): 44 docs, avg doc 6.1KB, total request body ~320KB
- Case C (succeeds 100%): 100 docs but doc text truncated to 1KB each

Request IDs (examples)
- us-east: req_01HT2ZK8Y4M6J4A8X9W2
- us-east: req_01HT31B2GQ9P2D7VJ8K1
- eu-west: req_01HT33P0A6JQ0K5R3N8M

Initial hypothesis
- Rerank worker OOM / memory pressure during tokenization or embedding of large batches (batch-size * sequence-length).
- Potentially exacerbated by large JSON payloads and/or long documents leading to very large token counts.

Interim workaround (to share with customer)
- Chunk rerank documents into batches of <= 50 documents (recommended starting point).
- If documents are long, truncate/summarize to <= ~1,500–2,000 characters per document before rerank.
- Add retry with exponential backoff on 5xx (max 2 retries) and log request_id for Support.
- If strict ordering is needed across chunks, rerank each chunk then merge via score normalization (customer-specific guidance).

Escalation criteria
- If 500 rate > 1% across multiple requests with <= 50 docs, or failures occur with small payloads, treat as P0/P1 and page on-call.

Next actions
- Validate in dashboards/logs for rerank fleet (OOM/restarts, p95 latency) around request IDs.
- File Eng bug with repro characteristics (batch size, doc length) and propose guardrails (max docs/max tokens) + clearer 4xx error if limits exceeded (instead of 500).
comments:
2026-02-12 10:14 PT — Priya Shah (Support)
Customer report received via ticket form. Asked for: region, approximate batch size, avg doc size, and 2–3 request IDs. Provided interim guidance to try <=50 docs per call while we investigate.

Shared with customer:
- "Can you try chunking to 25–50 docs per request and let us know if it stabilizes? If you share request_id values from failing calls, we can trace server-side logs."

2026-02-12 11:03 PT — Customer (Aurora Search)
Confirmed chunking to 50 docs eliminates 500s. Failures appear when docs > ~150 or when docs are ‘full page’ text. Provided request IDs (see description) and noted us-east is main region.

2026-02-12 11:22 PT — Owen Phillips (Support incidents)
Triaged as P1/Sev2 due to 5xx on prod endpoint with workaround. Pulled quick view dashboards: rerank error rate spike around 2026-02-11 21:00–23:00 UTC, correlated with pod restarts in us-east. Looping in SRE for confirmation of OOM pattern.

Action: created ENG-4833 to track guardrail/fix; added repro notes (batch size * doc length).

2026-02-12 12:05 PT — Allison Grant (SRE)
Confirmed in us-east rerank worker logs: multiple container OOMKills during tokenization burst; memory RSS climbs rapidly on large-batch requests. This maps to request IDs shared.

Tentative root cause:
- Large rerank batches create a very large tokenization buffer; workers restart mid-request, leading to gateway surfacing 500.

Mitigation options:
1) Short-term: enforce/advertise a safe max docs per request (and ideally return 413/422 with a clear message instead of 500).
2) Medium-term: cap tokenization memory usage / stream tokenization; improve batching behavior.

No immediate broader incident declared since workaround is effective and error rate is localized to large requests; monitoring continues.

2026-02-12 13:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support)
Updated customer with workaround + we are addressing server-side stability:
- Recommended <= 50 docs per rerank call
- If docs are long, truncate to <= 2k chars
- Capture request_id on any failures and send to Support

Also clarified:
- "We’ll follow up with a permanent fix and/or documented limits so this fails gracefully rather than returning a 500."

2026-02-13 09:18 PT — Mina Haddad (Platform)
Noted that gateway currently treats rerank upstream resets as generic 500. We should prefer a deterministic client error when inputs exceed safe limits.

Added suggestion to ENG-4833:
- Introduce server-side validation for max docs and/or estimated max tokens.
- Include request_id + actionable guidance in error body (chunk size recommendation).

2026-02-14 16:40 PT — Allison Grant (SRE)
Applied a config mitigation in us-east to reduce concurrent rerank batch processing and increase headroom. Observed fewer OOMKills, but this is not a complete fix if a single request is very large.

Recommendation remains: implement guardrails + fix tokenization memory behavior.

2026-02-16 10:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Support incidents)
Customer confirms workaround is holding (chunking to 40 docs; truncating long documents). No new 500s since 2026-02-13.

Marking SUP ticket Resolved with workaround; keeping ENG-4833 open for permanent fix and improved error handling. Added note to consider publishing as a Known Issue article if we see repeats this week.
resolution: Resolved via customer-side workaround (chunk rerank batches to <=50 docs and truncate long document texts). SRE confirmed root cause is rerank worker OOMKills triggered by large-batch tokenization/memory spikes; a partial server-side config mitigation reduced restarts but does not fully prevent single-request overload. Engineering follow-up tracked in ENG-4833 to add input guardrails and return a clear 4xx with guidance instead of 500, plus longer-term memory fixes.
